claims.text: When asked by NBC News correspondent Kelly O'Donnell what he envisioned bans on media outlets looking like, US President Donald Trump responded: 'Oh, the ban on the free press, right?'
Regarding his White House press ban, Donald Trump stated: 'I don't want them in my office. I don't want them here. I would say the ban would go as far as you can.'
US President Donald Trump stated he intends to sue CNN, Politico, and MS Now.
US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act into law on Friday.
The House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act in a bipartisan 262-159 vote two days before it was signed into law.
The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act allows the US president to impose tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy, including China.
The leaders of the US, Denmark, and Greenland announced on Friday that they expect to sign an Arctic security pact next week during the UN General Assembly.
US President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social on Friday that he is immediately banning CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House.
CNN called Donald Trump's White House ban an 'illegal assault' on fundamental, constitutionally-protected press freedoms.
Politico released a statement saying it 'will continue to fairly report on this White House and future ones' and will vigorously defend its First Amendment rights.
In February 2025, the White House took control of the press pool covering the president, ending over a century of management by the White House Correspondents Association.

In February 2025, the Trump administration barred Associated Press reporters and photographers from limited-access spaces after the agency continued using the term 'Gulf of Mexico' instead of 'Gulf of America'.

Jameel Jaffer, executive director of the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University, stated that the press pool is a 'public forum' under the First Amendment and excluding journalists based on viewpoint is unconstitutional.
Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, called President Trump's media ban 'flatly unconstitutional' and 'textbook viewpoint discrimination.'
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are banned from the White House due to their constant reporting of 'FAKE NEWS'.
Former US President Richard Nixon previously placed restrictions on the Washington Post over its reporting on the Watergate scandal.
Donald Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that banned outlets 'purposely write negative news' to try to diminish Republicans.
Reporters Without Borders stated it is appalled by Donald Trump's threat to ban news outlets and is exploring legal avenues to respond.
Donald Trump previously berated news outlets that reported on US munitions stockpiles being strained by the war on Iran as 'treasonous scum'.
Amnesty International posted on social media accusing the Trump administration of trying to 'stifle scrutiny and evade accountability' by punishing journalists.
The US and Denmark announced a security deal regarding Greenland to be signed at the United Nations General Assembly.
Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that the Greenland security agreement comes at 'no cost to the United States'.

Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen stated the security deal 'strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area' while recognizing the sovereignty of the Kingdom and Greenlandic self-determination.
Chairman of the Greenland Government Jens-Frederik Nielsen confirmed in a statement that Greenland, Denmark, and the US are about to enter into a security agreement.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the agreement a 'historic deal' and a 'huge win for the United States and the American people'.

An anonymous US State Department official stated the Greenland agreement explicitly guarantees the US complete ability to secure and defend the American continent, including permanent access, basing, and overflight rights.
A US State Department official stated the Greenland agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot set up bases or send troops to Greenland.
Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that plans will begin immediately to develop a large military presence in appropriate parts of Greenland.
Donald Trump referred to the Greenland security pact as an 'Infinite Life' agreement with no end date.
The United States currently maintains a military installation at Pituffik Space Base in Greenland under existing defense arrangements with Denmark.
A vehicle bomb explosion and gun attack on a mosque near police offices in Pakistan's Kohat district killed at least 21 people and injured 80.
Six armed gunmen and one suicide bomber involved in the Kohat compound attack were killed by police.
A roadside bomb struck a security forces convoy in Pakistan's Hangu district on Thursday, killing six soldiers.
Pakistani government troops killed 10 suspected Pakistani Taliban militants during raids on Thursday.
Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Lt. Gen. Asim Malik to discuss Afghanistan-Pakistan tensions.
Fifteen police officers and a four-year-old child were among those killed in the Kohat mosque suicide attack.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police suggested a faction of the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) carried out the attack in Kohat.
UN Secretary-General António Guterres strongly condemned the Kohat bombing, stating attacks targeting places of worship are unacceptable.
Pakistani security forces killed seven militants during two separate operations in Balochistan province.
In February, a suicide bombing at the Khadija Tul Kubra Mosque in Islamabad killed at least 31 people.
Thirty-seven suspected illegal gold miners died while held in custody in a cell operated by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, Niger state.
Police fired teargas at protesters and imposed an overnight 6pm curfew in Minna following demonstrations over the miners' deaths.
An intelligence report seen by AFP indicated that preliminary findings point to overcrowding and inadequate ventilation as the cause of death for the 37 miners.
Niger State Governor Umar Bago declared three days of mourning and postponed the start of election campaigning following the incident.
Nigeria Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo ordered the immediate suspension of Niger state NSCDC commandant Suberu Siyaka Aniviye pending an investigation.
The 37 deceased detainees were buried on Thursday according to Islamic tradition without forensic examinations being performed.
NSCDC spokesperson Babawale Afolabi stated that more than 50 people had been arrested in the raids prior to the deaths.
The NSCDC initially claimed the detainees may have died due to a diphtheria outbreak before later stating the cause of death was unconfirmed.
Security forces in Nigeria opened fire and deployed tear gas during a second day of protests in Minna on Friday.
Niger State Governor Umar Bago imposed a 24-hour curfew in response to violent protests targeting government buildings in Minna.
The Bank of Japan raised its target interest rate by 25 basis points to 1.25% in a 7-2 majority vote.
The Japanese yen fell against the US dollar following the Bank of Japan's rate hike announcement.
French football player Kylian Mbappe signed an endorsement deal with Swiss sportswear brand On, ending his long partnership with Nike.
The Bank of Japan's interest rate increase to 1.25% brings borrowing costs in Japan to their highest level since 1995.
Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda stated he would not rule out back-to-back interest rate hikes, noting it depends on how price conditions develop.
The rate of inflation in Japan was 1.9% in August.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned currency traders not to bet against the yen, stating he had insight into Japanese policy actions.
In late July, the US Treasury sold at least $10 billion in euros to buy yen and support the Japanese currency.
The Bank of England voted to hold UK interest rates unchanged at 3.75%.
